Texas A&M International University (TAMIU) has earned the Bronze Veterans Education Excellence Recognition Award from the Texas Veterans Commission, the first time in university history that TAMIU has received the distinction, according to the university.

The award honors colleges and universities that show a strong commitment to providing exceptional educational services, resources and support to veterans and members of the military-connected community.

University President Dr. Christopher Maynard called the recognition an important milestone that reflects TAMIU's commitment to making sure veterans and military-connected students have the support they need to succeed, according to TAMIU.

A key leader in the effort was University Registrar Triana Valdez, who oversees the university's Office of Veterans Affairs. Vice President of Enrollment Management Juan García credited Valdez's leadership and the work of the Veterans Affairs team for guiding the university through the process of pursuing the recognition, according to the university.

The Office of Veterans Affairs helps veteran and military-connected students navigate the educational benefits and resources available to them as they pursue their academic goals, and helps them understand and access those benefits and transition into and through their university experience.

Valdez said the award belongs to the entire campus community and reflects the team's dedication and the university's ongoing commitment to supporting veterans, according to TAMIU.

Veterans interested in continuing their academic careers at TAMIU can learn more about Office of Veterans Affairs services at tamiu.edu/veterans, by emailing veterans@tamiu.edu, by calling 956.326.2251, or by visiting the Senator Judith Zaffirini Student Success Center, room 121K.

Sources: Texas A&M International University.
